links.outcome: Reliability of LVO probability categories versus mathematical calibration; association with infarct volume and mRS
links.effect: Four-category recategorization (unlikely, less likely, possible, suggestive) gave a reliable LVO estimate compared with mathematical calibration, and categories were significantly associated with follow-up infarct volume and 3-month mRS.
links.quote: Due to sparse data between 20-60% of LVO probabilities, recategorization into unlikely (0-20% LVO scores), less likely (20-60%), possible (60-90%), and suggestive (90-100%) provided a reliable estimation of LVO compared with mathematical calibration.

screen.reason: Multicenter validation study evaluating deep learning software (JLK-LVO) for large vessel occlusion detection on CTA, which specifically tests post-processing risk categorization/calibration methods to map model output probabilities to clinically reliable categories.
